text:
Minnesota is 13-3-4, has points in nine straight, and has a 98% chance at the playoffs in our simulations. The bigger story is what comes after this season. Quinn Hughes tops Daily Faceoff's ranking of next summer's free agents, and the rumor columns have already started linking the Wild to Nikita Kucherov, who has asked out of Tampa, as a plan B if Hughes doesn't re-sign. The Athletic reports that Kirill Kaprizov and Kucherov would love to play together. That's a lot of noise around a team that is simply winning.

And winning in a way that mostly holds up. The Wild get 56% of the expected goals (the quality of chances). The Joel Eriksson Ek, Kaprizov and Matt Boldy line has outscored opponents 16-0 at five on five in 213 minutes, which is absurd, and Kaprizov's 16 goals lead the league. Hughes drives play with either Jonas Brodin or Jared Spurgeon.

The part to keep an eye on is Jesper Wallstedt. He leads the NHL in wins and saves, and over his last five starts he's at .931. Wild goalies have allowed 14 fewer goals than expected, which is why our numbers have Minnesota about five points ahead of what it deserved. Some of that is talent. Some of it will fade.

What to watch: the depth. Maxim Shabanov is running hot (7 points in 10) on a line that loses its minutes. If the top line ever cools, the Wild will need that line to hold.
headline: The Wild are rolling, and Quinn Hughes is the question
